July

The 14th to the 17th. Chapter one.

Four days in Salamanca. It's the shortest chapter on this page, and somehow it's the one everything else grew out of.

  1. Tuesday, July 14

    Under a tree

    I didn't sleep the night before. Too excited, and I had to be up early for my flight anyway, so I stayed on call with you from around 1am until it was time to catch my train to JFK. Then the flight, then an Uber, then an hour of trees and hills out the window on the way to Salamanca, plus a little bonus sleep in the back seat.

    I checked into the hotel, knocked out, and woke up rushing to get ready for our first date. A bit nervous, but way more excited. We met under a big tree, in matching outfits we definitely did not plan, and you were so cute and shy. Honestly, it was love at first sight. I still wish we'd taken a picture of us that day. Memory will do, but I drew one anyway.

    Over food at Seven Dragon, the shyness wore off on both sides, and we started talking like we'd known each other for years.

    After that we walked. All over Salamanca, no real plan, just exploring and talking. Tap the stops to retrace it.

    Tap a stop on our walk.

    Salamanca, through my camera.

  2. Wednesday, July 15

    The day we count from

    The day after our first perfect date, you felt safe and comfortable enough to come back to the room with me, and you told me you'd like to stay the night. Spending the day and night together was the best option, and not just because we were lowkey getting cooked by the weather. It was a chance to get closer and just relax, the two of us. We wound down, ordered takeout, watched movies, and I even gave you a little tour of the casino (again, that game room was waaay too overpriced, lmfao). And then our little addiction came into play… GAMBLING!

    🍒💗🍩
    flip me: switches modes

    Lever down: free spins, unlimited.

    One more spin. Just one.

    Later we went back to the room, hugged a bit more, and started on the detective crime case game I'd brought from Target. We both tried to figure it out, lol. Then we took a pause, and I finally asked the question I'd been wanting to ask you. I told you how I felt, and then I asked:

    "Will you be my girlfriend?" You said yes.

    We held each other. It felt like a fever dream, but it happened. After all that, we ordered takeout again and binge-watched movies, until we slowly got sleepy and fell asleep together, cuddling.

  3. Thursday, July 16

    Not enough time

    We woke up pretty late in the morning, and I woke up a little emotional. I didn't want this to be the last day, even though it was the last real one. You wanted to spend the morning outside so we could make more memories, and honestly I wanted to go out too, so you picked the museum. Part of me just wanted to keep you in my arms a little longer and hope I was still dreaming, but we went, and I really enjoyed it. We learned the whole story of how Salamanca was founded, how different it was back then, and how the Seneca Nation was here first, still is, and is still respected.

    After that little adventure we relaxed in bed together, and it started to hit us: the day was passing way too fast, and we wanted every bit of it to count. It hit me hardest that afternoon. I'd been keeping it all inside (fun fact: I actually cried a little the first night we spent together, haha). Then we started saying how much we wished we had more days, and you, my beautiful baby, started crying too. I tucked you into my chest, kissed your head, and told you it would be alright, wishing the whole time that we had more days. We got comfortable, cuddled, and passed out together until it was time to leave that evening.

    Then I walked you home so you'd get back safe. On the way we grabbed a Tim Hortons dozen box for your family, for the brownie points (EZ). It was a very long walk, but honestly an enjoyable one. When we got there we chatted with your mom, and everyone was lovely, including Taff, big ol' Mittens, and your siblings. It felt cozy, and the food was great.

    We'd planned to walk around the block to say our goodbyes, eye to eye, one more hug. Instead your dad cockblocked us, lol, and picked us up way too early to drive me back to the resort. On the car ride it was just me and your dad talking, and the start was lowkey rough and slow. So I used my ultimate.

    Final boss: your dad HP

    Quiet. Just got off work. Driving.

    Once we both settled down, we called, and we just got emotional. Honestly, it was hard for me. Once I got into my room I broke down and was already missing you. Not being able to see you in front of me, cuddled up close and sleeping well, is what hit me the hardest.

  4. Friday, July 17

    Midnight

    Right at midnight I headed out for Buffalo and a 6am flight back to the city. Four days. That's all it took, and I was already counting down to the next time.

One more time, for the date we count from.

Hold the button. Keep holding for more.

August

Summer, mostly over the phone.

After July, the distance came back, but it felt different. Summer turned into late calls, long texts, falling asleep mid-conversation, the "you still up?" hours. Catch the fireflies. Each one is carrying something we've said to each other.

    The leaves started dropping and two months snuck up on us. It doesn't feel like two months. It feels like I've known you a lot longer. There's a note buried under the pile. Clear it off: tap the leaves, or sweep your mouse across them.
